scenes.heading: Animal body plans
scenes.sub: Over a million species, a handful of designs
scenes.say: There are well over a million described animal species. But most are built on a few basic body plans: symmetry, tissue layers, body cavity, and how the embryo develops.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A pizza can be cut into matching halves in many directions
scenes.science: Radial animals have many mirror planes; bilateral animals have one
scenes.breaks: Cars are designed, but symmetry evolved. Sea stars are radial as adults but bilateral as larvae, showing bilateral ancestors.
scenes.say: A round pizza can be cut through the centre in many directions to give matching halves. That's radial symmetry, like a jellyfish. A car has only one mirror cut, front to back: bilateral symmetry. And like headlights on a car, sense organs cluster at the front. That's cephalisation.

scenes.heading: Germ layers
points: Ecto = exit: skin and nervous system
scenes.say: Gastrulation forms germ layers. Ecto means exit: the outside skin and nervous system. Endo means enter: the gut lining and organs like the liver. Meso means middle: muscle and most organs. Jellyfish have two layers. All bilateral animals have three.

scenes.heading: Body cavities
points: Fluid acts as a hydrostatic skeleton
scenes.say: Classify a body cavity by its lining. A coelom is fully lined by mesoderm. A pseudocoelom is only partly lined. Acoelomates, like flatworms, have no cavity. Like squeezing a water balloon, an earthworm's muscles push on the fluid to burrow.

scenes.heading: Protostomes vs deuterostomes
scenes.say: Protostome means first mouth: the blastopore becomes the mouth. Deuterostome means second mouth: it becomes the anus. You're a deuterostome, so your first opening was your bottom! Deuterostome cleavage is radial and indeterminate, which is why identical twins are possible.

scenes.heading: Identify the animal
scenes.question: Bilateral, three germ layers, true coelom, segmented with bristles, blastopore becomes mouth, spiral cleavage.
scenes.say: Use each feature to move down the tree. Bilateral with three layers: a bilaterian. Blastopore becomes the mouth with spiral cleavage: a protostome. A true coelom, segments and bristles, but no exoskeleton: it's an annelid, a marine worm.

scenes.heading: Survivorship curves
steps: Type II: steady death rate (many birds)
Trade-off: more offspring, less care each
scenes.say: Life histories involve trade-offs: energy spent on reproduction can't go to growth or survival. Survivorship curves: one live long, two steady, three die young. Type three species, like many fish, make huge numbers of offspring with little care.

points: Ecto exit, endo enter, meso middle
scenes.say: Quick recap. Symmetry is radial or bilateral. Remember the three germ layers. A coelom is fully lined by mesoderm. Protostomes are first mouth, deuterostomes second mouth. And chordates have a notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits and a tail. Now try the practice questions!
